questions.prompt: The old man whom the citizens revered died on a cloudy evening.
questions.answer: Senex quem cīvēs verēbantur vesperō nūbilō occidit.

questions.prompt: The blessings which we enjoy were given by benevolent gods.
questions.answer: Bona quibus fruimur ā deīs benevolīs data sunt.

questions.prompt: The mother into whose lap the infant had climbed was singing softly.
questions.answer: Māter in cuius gremium īnfāns ascenderat lēniter canēbat.

questions.prompt: The walls which the enemy destroyed had once been high.
questions.answer: Mūrī quōs hostis dēlēvit ōlim altī fuerant.

questions.prompt: The father and son who had been captured were led into the city.
questions.answer: Pater et fīlius quī captī erant in urbem ductī sunt.

questions.prompt: Folly and cowardice, which must be shunned, destroy many men.
questions.answer: Stultitia et timiditās, quae fugienda sunt, multōs perdunt.

questions.prompt: The honors and victories which are accidental do not last.
questions.answer: Honōrēs et victōriae quae sunt fortuīta nōn permanent.

questions.prompt: The mother and daughter whom we praised departed at dawn.
questions.answer: Māter et fīlia quās laudāvimus prīmā lūce discessērunt.

questions.prompt: The prison, which is called Lautumiae, held many captives.
questions.answer: Carcer, quae Lautumiae vocantur, multōs captīvōs tenēbat.

questions.prompt: He approached the animal which the Greeks call an elephant.
questions.answer: Ad animal quem elephantum vocant appropinquāvit.

questions.prompt: The Belgae, who are the third part, are the bravest.
questions.answer: Belgae, quae est tertia pars, fortissimī sunt.

questions.prompt: We reached the river which men call the Rhine.
questions.answer: Ad flūmen quem hominēs Rhēnum vocant pervēnimus.

questions.prompt: The poet to whom the king gave gifts wrote a long poem.
questions.answer: Poēta cui rēx dōna dedit longum carmen scrīpsit.

questions.prompt: The sword with which he killed the tyrant lay on the ground.
questions.answer: Gladius quō tyrannum occīdit in terrā iacēbat.

questions.prompt: The friends on whom we rely never abandon us.
questions.answer: Amīcī quibus confīdimus nōs numquam dēserunt.

questions.prompt: The soldier whose courage we admired fell in battle.
questions.answer: Mīles cuius virtūtem mīrābāmur in proeliō cecidit.

questions.prompt: A part of the men, who had been thrown to the beasts, perished.
questions.answer: Pars hominum, quī bēstiīs obiectī erant, periērunt.

questions.prompt: The crowd, who were shouting in a loud voice, rushed into the forum.
questions.answer: Turba, quī magnā vōce clāmābant, in forum ruērunt.

questions.prompt: The army, whom the general praised, returned home as victors.
questions.answer: Exercitus, quōs dux laudāvit, victōrēs domum revertērunt.

questions.prompt: The youth, who were eager for war, seized their weapons.
questions.answer: Iuventūs, quī bellī cupidī erant, arma rapuērunt.

questions.prompt: The letter which had been sent by the consul frightened everyone.
questions.answer: Epistula quae ā cōnsule missa erat omnēs terruit.

questions.prompt: The trees which the wind had thrown down were blocking the road.
questions.answer: Arborēs quās ventus dēiēcerat viam obstruēbant.

questions.prompt: The wine which we drank at dinner was excellent.
questions.answer: Vīnum quod in cēnā bibimus optimum erat.

questions.prompt: The experiment which the philosopher attempted was in vain.
questions.answer: Experīmentum quod philosophus temptāvit irritum fuit.
